overall_summary: Analysis of the deduplicated performance metrics shows that extreme space and astronomical 'What If' scenarios (particularly involving exotic planets, extreme environments, and hypothetical immersive scenarios) generate the highest views-per-day and engagement (likes-per-view) among recent 7-day uploads. Titles using hypothetical immersive questions ('What If You Fell Into...') and bizarre planetary physics ('Liquid Diamond Planet', 'Venus Has a Day Longer Than Its Year') significantly outperform standard biological facts or historical mysteries.

winning_patterns.evidence: Videos like 'What If You Fell Into a Liquid Diamond Planet?' (IYuce8vaU3Y) and 'What If You Fell Into the Planet of Burning Ice?' (8KEl0_pJ_68) garnered over 1,000 and 972 views rapidly with strong like-to-view ratios.
winning_patterns.action: Double down on 'What If' interactive physics scenarios focused on extreme celestial bodies.

winning_patterns.evidence: Videos like 'Venus Has a Day Longer Than Its Year 🤯' (A9Qa-RmuOr0) and 'The Planet Darker Than Coal: TrES-2b 🌌' (v1rrcZLdp4U) achieved rapid traction exceeding 900-1,000 views within days.
winning_patterns.action: Produce more short-form concepts focusing on bizarre, counter-intuitive laws of physics operating on newly discovered exoplanets.

weak_patterns.evidence: Topics like 'Your Brain Can Create Fake Memories' (2fqaGqfsR4A) and song-stuck psychological tricks stalled heavily at under 60 views with zero engagement.
weak_patterns.action: De-prioritize basic psychology factoids unless framed as high-stakes narrative mysteries.

weak_patterns.evidence: Standard animal facts such as 'Octopuses Have THREE Hearts' (when repeated or aged) show diminishing returns compared to space content.
weak_patterns.action: Pivot animal content into cinematic survival or extreme evolutionary anomalies rather than basic trivia.
